correctness.rationale: Six explicit 11-cyclic pentads generate 66 distinct blocks covering each of 330 tetrads once. Block intersection counts (15,20,30 at sizes 1,2,3, none at size 0) and five distinct forbidden extensions of every nonblock pentad prove that the 66 free hexad facets are exactly complements of blocks, giving K*=K. Exact enumeration gives f=(11,55,165,330,396,66) and 1023 nonempty faces. The supplied checker constructs a 451-pair discrete-Morse matching with one critical vertex and 120 critical 4-cells and checks all 4301 oriented face incidences are acyclic by a complete 1023-node topological sort. The resulting CW model has no possible nontrivial attaching maps, so its homotopy type is a wedge of 120 4-spheres. Executable verifier and output are embedded and replayed.

originality.rationale: The full-text Witt existence/construction source specifies the Steiner incidence object, not its block-avoidance topology. Ballico et al. discuss Stanley-Reisner and matroid complexes generated by complements of NONblocks and algebraic graded Betti numbers, different from the present complex with complements of BLOCKS as facets. Public indexed-result searches for Witt pentads, Mathieu M11, Alexander self-duality, hypergraph independence and the exact 120-sphere homotopy yielded no matching or dominating theorem. Closest thematic mathematical records concern different designs/complexes and cannot directly imply this result. Absence of indexed matches does not prove absolute priority.

value.rationale: The unique Mathieu-symmetric Witt 4-design is a canonical, historically central hypergraph. Its block-avoidance complex is natural and previously not determined by the cited design existence/count theorems; the result gives both a striking exact Alexander self-duality and the FULL integral homotopy type (120 four-spheres despite five-dimensional facets). This complete finite classification gives a reproducible topological benchmark for Steiner-system hypergraph independence complexes, beyond the easy counts and beyond a torsion-free homology calculation.
